title: U.S. House · Florida's 4th District
area: Northeast Florida including Jacksonville's northern suburbs, Nassau County and parts of Duval and St. Johns counties.

context.text: Incumbent Aaron Bean's Republican primary was canceled and he advanced unopposed. LaShonda Holloway won the Democratic primary over Michael Kirwan and Brittney Robinson; this is her third consecutive run for this seat, having lost to Bean in 2022 and 2024. Mike Sell (Florida Forward Party) and Todd Schaefer (No Party Affiliation) also qualified for the general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Aaron Bean
candidates.ballotNote: Republican primary was canceled; advanced unopposed.

summary.text: Aaron Bean is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Florida's 4th District. He previously served in the Florida House of Representatives (2000-2008) and Florida Senate (2012-2022), and as mayor and a commissioner of Fernandina Beach.

background.text: Born in Fernandina Beach, Florida; earned a B.S. in finance from Jacksonville University in 1989.
Worked as an auctioneer and as a relationship development officer with UF Health Jacksonville.
Served as mayor and a commissioner of the City of Fernandina Beach (1996-1999), in the Florida House (2000-2008), and in the Florida Senate (2012-2022).

Chaired the Early Childhood, Elementary, and Secondary Education subcommittee of the Committee on Education and the Workforce, and served on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Small Business, during the 118th Congress (2023-2024); in the 119th Congress (2025-2026) he sits on the Committee on Ways and Means, including the Subcommittees on Social Security, Work and Welfare, and Oversight.

priorities.text: Says the Working Families Tax Cut strengthens Medicaid's accountability, efficiency, and access while ensuring taxpayer dollars are spent wisely, rather than cutting the program.
Education: co-led a Parents Roundtable and joined the introduction of the Parents Bill of Rights as chair of the Early Childhood, Elementary, and Secondary Education Subcommittee.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means, including the Subcommittees on Social Security, Work and Welfare, and Oversight, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: Federal roll-call votes and FEC finance totals for this sitting member are added by script. Bean's official House issues subpages (Economy, Education, Energy, Health, Veterans) are mostly placeholder text pointing to press releases rather than stated positions; his 'Working Families Tax Cut FAQs' initiative page was the main source of a position in his own words.

candidates.name: LaShonda Holloway
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary over Michael Kirwan and Brittney Robinson. This is her third consecutive general-election run for this seat, having lost to Bean in 2022 (39.5%) and 2024 (42.7%).

summary.text: LaShonda Holloway is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 4th Congressional District, making her third consecutive run against incumbent Aaron Bean. She holds a J.D. from the University of Florida College of Law.

background.text: Born in Florida; graduated from Edward Waters College in 1997 and earned a J.D. from the University of Florida College of Law.

priorities.text: Education: legislation to decrease the financial burden of higher education.
Healthcare: expanding coverage, preventive care and access to mental health services.
Communities: access to food, employment, healthcare and affordable housing.

positions.summary: Her 2024 campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia, supports universal access to reproductive healthcare including safe, legal abortion.
positions.quote: Additionally, supporting policies that ensure universal access to reproductive healthcare, including essential services such as birth control, prenatal care, and safe, legal abortion is imperative.

candidates.researchNotes: Her campaign site (copyright 2024) lists platform topics such as Fair Living Wage and Affordable Housing without detailing positions; her News4JAX questionnaire left the issues question blank. No debate or forum coverage found. Her abortion and healthcare positions are from her 2024 site as quoted by Ballotpedia.

statements.quote: As lawmakers, we must be committed to expanding healthcare coverage, promoting preventative care initiatives, and increasing access to mental health services to ensure that every individual receives the care they need to thrive.

candidates.name: Mike Sell

summary.text: Mike Sell is the Florida Forward Party nominee for Florida's 4th Congressional District. He built a career in healthcare operational-excellence work and says he takes no corporate money.

background.text: Raised in a Navy family; started working in high school and built a career in operational excellence, mostly within the U.S. healthcare industry, earning a Six Sigma Black Belt certification.
Founded a not-for-profit built on the belief that access to information is a right, and has worked on diversity programs and community volunteering.

priorities.text: Says he takes no corporate money and answers to no party machine.
priorities.quote: I take no corporate money and answer to no party machine. My time and my loyalty belong to the people of this district, not to donors I would owe before ever taking office.

priorities.text: Making life more affordable: higher wages and ending price gouging on rent, groceries, healthcare and prescriptions.
Fixing the political system: getting money out of politics, fair district maps, real accountability and term limits.

statements.context: In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

statements.quote: Ask the wealthiest to pay their fair share
statements.context: In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

candidates.researchNotes: Statements are short policy-list items from his 2026 Ballotpedia survey and campaign site (the site also has an AI chatbot, not used). No fuller explanation of any item was found.

candidates.name: Todd Schaefer

summary.text: Todd Schaefer is a no-party-affiliation candidate for Florida's 4th Congressional District and a retired Navy service member, running against what he calls a two-party system that isn't working for voters.

priorities.text: Wants to reduce the influence of big-dollar donors on both major parties.
Says the U.S. should refocus resources at home rather than on foreign military spending, citing the defense funding in the 'One Big Beautiful Bill' (OBBB).

positions.summary: In a News4JAX questionnaire he calls for expanding Medicare to a public option.
positions.quote: The logic of that leads to a national public option, since the largest possible pool is the whole country. Any legislation to continue subsidies has to include language to expand Medicare to a public option.

positions.summary: In his 2025 Ballotpedia survey he lists a minimum wage that is not out of date and is tied to inflation as a policy priority; his campaign site says the same.
positions.quote: A minimum wage that isn't 16 years out of date and a way to tie it to inflation

statements.quote: We've also weaponized the US Dollar against countries we don't agree with through sanctions and tariffs.
statements.context: On his campaign issues page, under Diplomatic Foreign Policy Solutions

statements.quote: We don't need more subsidies that inflate prices further. We need to attack the root causes, restore balance between shelter and investment, and support local supply and first-time buyers through transparency and competition.
statements.context: On his campaign site's housing affordability page

candidates.researchNotes: Positions are from his campaign issues page, 2025 Ballotpedia survey and a July 2026 News4JAX questionnaire. The housing quote is from his housing page (toddforfl4.com/issues/housing-affordability); no statements found on abortion, guns, immigration or climate.
